newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks forecast strong on Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks forecast strong on Greenspan.

text.p: European stock markets are likely to open strongly on Wednesday after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sent Wall Street soaring to a record high by indicating American interest rates would not rise soon.

Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress on Tuesday was devoid of any mentions of market bubbles and irrational exuberance, the sort of comments that sent financial markets reeling last December.
But, speaking after European markets closed, Greenspan's comments were cautious.
"I have no doubt that the current stance of policy...will need to be changed at some point," he said in prepared testimony to a House Banking subcommittee.

"For the present, as I indicated, demand growth does appear to have moderated, but whether that moderation will be sufficient to avoid putting additional pressures on resources is an open question," he said.
Wall Street, hit by profit taking in recent sessions, saw Greenspan's comments as the green light to buy.

The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 154.93 points, or 1.96 percent, to 8,061.65, beating last Wednesday's record finish of 8,038.88. It was also the Dow's fourth biggest gain in history.
In London, dealers expected the FTSE-100 index to open sharply higher on Wednesday. Some dealers forecast a 40 point rise on the blue chip index.

Dealers said however that gains in London would be capped by caution before British June retail sales data due out at 0830 GMT and seen rising 0.4 percent. An auction of government bonds would also add to the caution.

"Greenspan will push the market up but there will be bated breath before the data and the gilts auction," said one dealer. The FTSE 100 finished 41.9 points higher on Tuesday at 4,899.3 after two days of gains.
"We will be squeezed up further," another dealer said. "What is going on yesterday and the day before is going to continue for the time being."

Continental markets should also be strong after Germany roared to a record close on Tuesday amid speculation of bank mergers and a weak mark, due to expectations that the single European currency will be soft.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar made a firm start against the mark in Europe, buoyed from its overnight gains by Greenspan's comments that, for now, U.S. growth seemed to be slowing.
The dollar climbed to 1.8245 marks in New York trade, its highest level since August 1991. It calmed down in Asian trade but was climbing back above 1.82 marks in early European dealings.
